q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores are ordinarily purchased only against provision of funds in the Stores Budget, the availability of funds being checked at the stage of vetting of the indent.
2. A purchase of stores can be sanctioned first and the provision of funds arranged afterwards in every case.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct - stores are purchased only against provision of funds in the Stores Budget, and the availability of funds is checked when the indent is vetted. Statement 2 is wrong - sanction first and funds afterwards is not permissible as a rule.

q: A stores depot issues 525 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 58 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Issue value = quantity issued x book rate = 525 x Rs 58 = Rs 30,450, debited to the consuming department at the book (average) rate of the item.

q: In stores parlance, the quantity of an item actually found in a depot on physical verification, as distinct from the balance shown in the records, is referred to as its:
e: The balance actually found on the ground during physical verification is the ground balance; it is compared with the book balance to bring out excesses and shortages.

q: A supplier fails to supply 900 units of stores contracted at Rs 68 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 81 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost = quantity x (risk purchase rate - contract rate) = 900 x (Rs 81 - Rs 68) = 900 x Rs 13 = Rs 11,700, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: Five wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 4 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 1,000 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Demurrage = wagons x days detained beyond free time x rate = 5 x 4 x Rs 1,000 = Rs 20,000.

q: A firm which is exempted from payment of Earnest Money Deposit in a stores tender is, on acceptance of its tender:

options.A: Also exempted from furnishing the Security Deposit
options.B: Required to furnish only half the prescribed Security Deposit
options.C: Still required to furnish the prescribed Security Deposit
options.D: Required to furnish double the prescribed Security Deposit

e: Exemption from Earnest Money Deposit does not carry exemption from Security Deposit; the successful tenderer must still furnish the prescribed SD to secure performance of the contract.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 15 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 38 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 44 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:
e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit + bills paid - material received and linked = 15 + 38 - 44 = Rs 9 lakh (debit), representing payments still awaiting linkage with receipts.

q: A depot holds 1,750 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 72 to Rs 80 per unit. The increase in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Increase in stock value = quantity in hand x rise in book rate = 1,750 x (Rs 80 - Rs 72) = 1,750 x Rs 8 = Rs 14,000, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 4,200 units and its book rate is Rs 175 per unit. For the purposes of ABC analysis, the annual consumption value of the item is:
e: Annual consumption value = annual consumption x unit (book) rate = 4,200 x Rs 175 = Rs 7,35,000; items are ranked on this value for ABC analysis.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 7,500 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 500 units. The number of orders to be placed during the year is:
e: Number of orders per year = annual requirement / EOQ = 7,500 / 500 = 15 orders.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 5,600 units and its Economic Order Quantity is 700 units. If the cost of placing one order is Rs 225, the total ordering cost per year is:
e: Orders per year = 5,600 / 700 = 8; total ordering cost = 8 x Rs 225 = Rs 1,800.

q: The average consumption of an item is 220 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 7 weeks. The consumption of the item during the lead time is:
e: Lead time consumption = average consumption per week x lead time in weeks = 220 x 7 = 1,540 units.

q: The average consumption of an item is 85 units per day and the lead time for emergency procurement is 4 days. The danger level of the item is:
e: Danger level = average daily consumption x lead time for emergency procurement = 85 x 4 = 340 units; when stock falls to this level, urgent action is needed to avoid a stock-out.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 6,050 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. Ordering at the Economic Order Quantity, the total of the annual ordering cost and the annual carrying cost is:
e: EOQ = sqrt(2 x 6,050 x 100 / 4) = 550 units. At EOQ, annual ordering cost (11 orders x Rs 100 = Rs 1,100) equals annual carrying cost (550/2 x Rs 4 = Rs 1,100), so the total is Rs 2,200.

q: When a stores item is deleted from the Priced Vocabulary of a railway, its PL number is:

options.A: Immediately allotted to a newly introduced item
options.B: Not re-allotted to any other item, so that the past records of the item remain unambiguous
options.C: Transferred to the list of non-stock items
options.D: Allotted to the depot's imprest stores

e: The PL number of a deleted item is not re-allotted to any other item, so that the past records and ledger entries of the deleted item remain unambiguous and traceable.

q: The abbreviation RDSO, the organisation which approves sources for safety and critical stores items, stands for:
e: RDSO stands for Research Designs and Standards Organisation; it is the organisation which approves sources and vendors for safety and critical stores items on the Railways.

q: The Indian Railway Stores Code, containing the rules for the purchase, custody, accounting and disposal of stores, is issued by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation

e: The Indian Railway Stores Code, containing the rules for purchase, custody, accounting and disposal of stores, is issued by the Railway Board.

q: Rate contracts for common-user goods and services, which were earlier concluded by the Directorate General of Supplies and Disposals (DGS&D), are now available to Government buyers on:
e: After the DGS&D rate contracts were discontinued, rate contracts for common-user goods and services became available to Government buyers on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM).

q: On the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), a buyer can procure goods and services through:

options.D: Direct purchase, bidding and reverse auction

e: GeM offers three modes of procurement - direct purchase, bidding and reverse auction - and the buyer adopts the mode appropriate to the value and nature of the procurement.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a limited tender for stores, invitations to tender are sent only to firms borne on the approved list of suppliers for the item.
2. In an open tender for stores, only firms registered with the Railways are permitted to submit offers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct - in a limited tender, invitations go only to firms borne on the approved list for the item. Statement 2 is wrong - an open tender is open to all firms, not only those registered with the Railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The net balance accumulated in the Stock Adjustment Account during a year is finally cleared by transfer to the revenue or capital heads concerned.
2. A debit balance under 'Sales Suspense' represents the money deposited by purchasers of scrap for which material is yet to be delivered to them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct - the net balance accumulated in the Stock Adjustment Account during the year is finally cleared to the revenue or capital heads concerned. Statement 2 is wrong - money deposited by scrap purchasers gives Sales Suspense a credit balance, not a debit balance.

q: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) in a stores tender differs from the Security Deposit (SD) in that the EMD is:

options.A: Furnished only by the successful tenderer after acceptance of the tender
options.B: Worked out as a percentage of the value of stores supplied during the year
options.C: Refunded only after the completion of the supplies under the contract
options.D: Furnished along with the tender by the tenderers, whereas the SD is furnished by the successful tenderer after acceptance of the tender

e: EMD is furnished by all tenderers along with the tender to ensure the seriousness of the bid, whereas Security Deposit is furnished only by the successful tenderer after acceptance of the tender, to secure performance of the contract.

q: Where a supplier despatches stores to a consignee depot by rail, the Railway Receipt (RR) for the consignment is sent to the consignee depot primarily to enable it to:

options.A: Pass the supplier's bill for payment
options.B: Take delivery of the consignment on its arrival
options.C: Prepare the priced stores ledger folio of the item
options.D: Fix the book rate of the item received

e: The Railway Receipt is sent to the consignee depot so that it can take delivery of the consignment from the carrying railway on its arrival at the destination station.

q: All material received at a stores depot from suppliers or other sources is, in the first instance, entered by the depot in the:
e: All material received at a depot is first entered in the Daily Receipt Register before it is inspected, taken into stock and posted in the priced stores ledger.

q: For easy location, identification and correct accounting, stores received in a depot are arranged and stocked:

options.A: According to their Price Ledger (PL) numbers
options.B: In the order in which they are received
options.C: According to the names of the suppliers
options.D: According to the dates of their purchase orders

e: Stores are arranged and stocked in the depot according to their Price Ledger (PL) numbers, so that each item can be readily located, identified and accounted for under its own PL folio.

q: Under the 'first in, first out' (FIFO) method followed for issuing stores from a depot:

options.A: The stock received earliest is issued first
options.B: The stock of the highest value is issued first
options.C: The stock received last is issued first
options.D: Issues are made in the order of the PL numbers of the items

e: Under FIFO, the stock received earliest is issued first, so that the oldest material is consumed before it deteriorates in store or becomes obsolete.

q: 'Surplus' stores in a depot are distinguished from 'dead surplus' stores in that surplus stores are those which:

options.A: Have not been issued at all during the preceding 24 months
options.B: Are in excess of the requirements of the holding depot but may be required by other depots, whereas dead surplus stores are neither used nor expected to be used within the prescribed periods
options.C: Have been condemned by the survey committee
options.D: Are held under the Sales Suspense head pending disposal

e: Surplus stores are in excess of the holding depot's requirements but may be required by other depots, so they are transferred; dead surplus stores are neither used nor expected to be used within the prescribed periods and are disposed of.

q: The average consumption of an item is 130 units per week, the lead time for its procurement is 6 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock provided for it is 260 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = (average consumption x lead time) + safety stock = (130 x 6) + 260 = 780 + 260 = 1,040 units.

q: The principal advantage of centralised purchase of stores at the headquarters or Railway Board level is that it secures:

options.A: Bulk-buying economies and uniformity of specifications and rates
options.B: Faster delivery of stores to the depots
options.C: Elimination of the need for stock verification

e: Centralised purchase pools the requirements of all depots at one level, securing bulk-buying economies together with uniformity of specifications and rates across the railway.

q: In the evaluation of stores tenders, the expression 'L1' denotes the tenderer:

options.A: Whose evaluated offer is the lowest
options.C: Who is borne at serial number one of the approved list
options.D: Who has quoted for the largest quantity

e: L1 denotes the tenderer whose evaluated offer is the lowest; subject to the offer being otherwise acceptable, the contract is ordinarily placed on the L1 tenderer.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 64 lakh and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 4 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance of stores / total issues = Rs 64 lakh / Rs 4 crore = 0.16; a lower ratio indicates faster-moving and healthier stock.

q: Which of the following is NOT a suspense or adjustment head operated in the Stores Accounts of a railway?
e: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is a suspense head of Workshop Accounts, operated for jobs executed in workshops; the Stores Accounts suspense heads are Purchase Suspense, Sales Suspense and Stores Miscellaneous Suspense.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 3,75,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98% of the bill value = 0.98 x Rs 3,75,000 = Rs 3,67,500, paid against the inspection certificate and despatch documents; the balance is paid on receipt and acceptance of the material.

q: A survey committee appointed for the condemnation and disposal of unserviceable stores ordinarily consists of representatives of:

options.B: The supplier firms which had supplied the stores
options.C: The Stores Department, the user department and the Accounts/Finance Department
options.D: The Railway Protection Force and the user department

e: The survey committee for condemnation and disposal of unserviceable stores ordinarily consists of representatives of the Stores Department, the user department and the Accounts/Finance Department, so that all aspects are examined.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 2,50,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 6 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5% of the value of stores in arrear for each week of delay = 0.005 x Rs 2,50,000 x 6 = Rs 7,500.

q: Track materials such as rails, sleepers and fittings required for the maintenance and renewal of track are stocked in depots known as:

options.D: Imprest stores held by field officials

e: Track materials such as rails, sleepers and fittings for maintenance and renewal of track are stocked in P-Way (Permanent Way) stores depots attached to the track organisation.

q: A depot holds 700 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 18 per unit. A fresh receipt of 300 units is taken into stock at Rs 28 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised book (average) rate = total value / total quantity = (700 x Rs 18 + 300 x Rs 28) / 1,000 = Rs 21,000 / 1,000 = Rs 21 per unit.

q: Stores held in a depot in excess of its own foreseeable requirements, which are available for transfer to other depots requiring them, are described as:
e: Stores held in excess of a depot's own foreseeable requirements, which other depots can use, are surplus stores; they are advised to other depots for transfer, unlike dead surplus which no depot requires.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 2,450 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 50 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 2 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = sqrt(2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost per unit) = sqrt(2 x 2,450 x 50 / 2) = sqrt(1,22,500) = 350 units.

q: In the integrated Material Management System (iMMS) of the Railways, the abbreviation 'UDM' stands for:
e: In the integrated Material Management System (iMMS), UDM stands for User Depot Module, the module through which user depots transact their stores demands.

q: The AAC of an item is 5,400 units. The stock in hand is 650 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 250 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Coverage = (stock in hand + dues) / AAC x 12 = (650 + 250) / 5,400 x 12 = 2 months of the anticipated annual consumption.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores found physically in excess of the book balance during stock verification are taken into stock, the value being credited to the Stock Adjustment Account.
2. A shortage of stores found during stock verification is written off from the books forthwith, without any enquiry or the sanction of the competent authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct - excesses found on verification are taken into stock with credit to the Stock Adjustment Account. Statement 2 is wrong - a shortage is investigated and written off only under the sanction of the competent authority, not forthwith.

q: The AAC of an item is 12,000 units. Coverage for three months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 1,300 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 700 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Quantity to order = requirement for 3 months - stock - dues = (12,000 x 3/12) - 1,300 - 700 = 3,000 - 2,000 = 1,000 units.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised mode of disposal of surplus or unserviceable stores on the Railways?

options.A: Transfer to another depot or railway requiring the stores
options.C: Return to the original supplier as a matter of course at the purchase price

e: Surplus or unserviceable stores are disposed of by transfer to another depot or railway, sale through e-auction, or sale to other Government departments; return to the original supplier at the purchase price as a matter of course is not a recognised mode.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,550 units and the re-order quantity is 700 units. The minimum consumption is 35 units per week and the minimum lead time is 4 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,550 + 700 - (35 x 4) = 2,110 units.

q: Which of the following statements about the procurement of stock and non-stock items is correct?

options.A: Stock items are procured against specific demands of works, and non-stock items against the AAC of the depot
options.B: Both stock and non-stock items are procured only through rate contracts
options.C: Non-stock items are first taken into the priced stock of the depot and issued later as required
options.D: Stock items are procured by the purchase office on the basis of depot indents linked to the AAC and coverage, while non-stock items are procured against specific demands

e: Stock items are held in depot stock and are procured by the purchase office against depot indents based on the AAC and coverage; non-stock items are not stocked and are procured only against specific demands.

q: The re-order level of an item is 950 units. The average consumption is 55 units per week and the average lead time is 6 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum stock level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 950 - (55 x 6) = 950 - 330 = 620 units.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 12,500 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 125 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 8 per unit per year. When orders are placed in Economic Order Quantities, the total of the annual ordering cost and the annual carrying cost is:
e: EOQ = sqrt(2 x 12,500 x 125 / 8) = 625 units. At EOQ, ordering cost (20 orders x Rs 125 = Rs 2,500) equals carrying cost (625/2 x Rs 8 = Rs 2,500), so the total is Rs 5,000.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 320 units per week, its normal consumption is 240 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 4 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (320 - 240) x 4 = 320 units, held to cover consumption above the normal rate during the lead time.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 25 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 62 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 58 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:
e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit + bills paid - material received and linked = 25 + 62 - 58 = Rs 29 lakh (debit).

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.15 crore, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 3.05 crore and issues during the year are Rs 3.30 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance of stores = opening balance + receipts - issues = 1.15 + 3.05 - 3.30 = Rs 0.90 crore = Rs 90 lakh.

q: A stores depot issues 875 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 44 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Issue value = quantity issued x book rate = 875 x Rs 44 = Rs 38,500, debited to the consuming department at the book (average) rate.

q: A supplier fails to supply 750 units of stores contracted at Rs 105 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 122 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost = quantity x (risk purchase rate - contract rate) = 750 x (Rs 122 - Rs 105) = 750 x Rs 17 = Rs 12,750, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: Three wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 5 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 1,100 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Demurrage = wagons x days detained beyond free time x rate = 3 x 5 x Rs 1,100 = Rs 16,500.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 95 lakh. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 20 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual inventory carrying cost = average stock value x carrying cost rate = Rs 95 lakh x 20% = Rs 19 lakh.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 13,200 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 1,200 units. If the cost of placing one order is Rs 250, the total ordering cost per year is:
e: Orders per year = annual requirement / EOQ = 13,200 / 1,200 = 11; total ordering cost = 11 x Rs 250 = Rs 2,750.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 850 units and a safety stock of 250 units. Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the average inventory of the item held is:
e: Average inventory = EOQ/2 + safety stock = 850/2 + 250 = 425 + 250 = 675 units; under uniform consumption the cycle stock averages half the order quantity.

q: The safety (buffer) stock of an item is 450 units and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 12 per unit per year. The annual carrying cost attributable to the safety stock is:
e: Annual carrying cost of the safety stock = safety stock x carrying cost per unit = 450 x Rs 12 = Rs 5,400.

q: During stock verification, 36 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 220 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Value of the excess = units found excess x book rate = 36 x Rs 220 = Rs 7,920, taken into stock with credit to the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A purchase order is placed on a supplier for stores valued at Rs 4,50,000. The security deposit prescribed under the contract at 5 per cent of the order value works out to:
e: Security Deposit = 5% of the order value = 0.05 x Rs 4,50,000 = Rs 22,500.

q: Under the General Financial Rules, the Earnest Money Deposit taken from tenderers in a procurement is referred to as:
e: Under the General Financial Rules, the Earnest Money Deposit furnished by tenderers with their bids is referred to as Bid Security, as distinct from the Performance Security furnished by the successful tenderer.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 8,100 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 50 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = sqrt(2 x 8,100 x 50 / 4) = sqrt(2,02,500) = 450 units, the order quantity at which the annual ordering and carrying costs balance.

q: Before a firm is approved by RDSO as a vendor for the supply of a safety or critical stores item, the firm is required to obtain approval of its:
e: Before RDSO approves a firm as a vendor for a safety or critical item, the firm's Quality Assurance Programme (QAP) must be approved, so that the system for assuring quality of manufacture and supply is established.

q: The average consumption of an item is 140 units per week, the lead time for its procurement is 7 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock provided for it is 420 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = (average consumption x lead time) + safety stock = (140 x 7) + 420 = 980 + 420 = 1,400 units.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 22 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 325 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Value of the shortage = units short x book rate = 22 x Rs 325 = Rs 7,150, to be accounted for through the Stock Adjustment Account pending investigation and write-off.

q: For the period for which the Earnest Money Deposit and the Security Deposit of a supplier remain with the Railways under a stores contract:

options.A: Interest is payable on both at the bank rate
options.B: Interest is payable only on the Security Deposit
options.C: No interest is payable by the Railways on either amount
options.D: Interest is payable only if the supplies are completed before time

e: No interest is payable by the Railways on Earnest Money Deposit or on Security Deposit for the period for which these amounts remain with the Railways under a stores contract.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 54 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 3 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance of stores / total issues = Rs 54 lakh / Rs 3 crore = 0.18.

q: A depot holds 900 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 22 per unit. A fresh receipt of 600 units is taken into stock at Rs 37 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised book (average) rate = (900 x Rs 22 + 600 x Rs 37) / 1,500 = Rs 42,000 / 1,500 = Rs 28 per unit.

q: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, tender sets (documents) are issued to micro and small enterprises participating in a procurement:

options.D: Only against their Earnest Money Deposit

e: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, tender sets (documents) are issued free of cost to micro and small enterprises participating in a procurement.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 175 units per week, its normal consumption is 125 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 8 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (175 - 125) x 8 = 400 units.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 2,75,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98% of the bill value = 0.98 x Rs 2,75,000 = Rs 2,69,500; the balance 2% is paid after receipt and acceptance of the material at the consignee depot.

q: Stores obtained by one depot from another depot on a 'loan' basis, as distinct from stores obtained on transfer, are those which:

options.A: Are permanently taken over by the receiving depot
options.B: Are paid for by the receiving depot at market rates
options.C: Are not accounted for in the books of either depot
options.D: Have to be returned to the lending depot or replaced by it in due course

e: Stores obtained on loan from another depot are not permanently taken over; they have to be returned to the lending depot or replaced by it in due course, unlike stores obtained on transfer.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 18 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 42 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 47 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:
e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit + bills paid - material received and linked = 18 + 42 - 47 = Rs 13 lakh (debit).

q: A depot holds an opening stock of 1,450 units of an item. During the year, 950 units are received into stock and 1,700 units are issued. The book rate of the item is Rs 40 per unit. The value of the closing stock of the item is:
e: Closing stock quantity = 1,450 + 950 - 1,700 = 700 units; value of closing stock = 700 x Rs 40 = Rs 28,000.

q: Issues of stores from railway depots are priced at the average (book) rate of the item. Which of the following pricing methods is NOT followed on the Railways?

options.B: First In, First Out (FIFO) for physical issue of stores
options.C: Weighted average (book) rate for pricing issues
options.D: Uniform issue rate at all depots of the railway

e: On the Railways, issues are priced at the weighted average (book) rate and physical issues follow FIFO; the Last In, First Out (LIFO) method is not followed.

q: The re-order level of an item is 2,300 units and the re-order quantity is 1,400 units. The minimum consumption is 65 units per week and the minimum lead time is 7 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 2,300 + 1,400 - (65 x 7) = 3,245 units.

q: A supplier fails to supply 650 units of stores contracted at Rs 92 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 108 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost = quantity x (risk purchase rate - contract rate) = 650 x (Rs 108 - Rs 92) = 650 x Rs 16 = Rs 10,400, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: The Security Deposit under a stores contract is required to be furnished by the successful tenderer:

options.A: Within 7 days of the opening of tenders
options.C: Within 21 days of the issue of the letter of acceptance of the tender
options.D: Only after the supplies are completed

e: The successful tenderer is required to furnish the Security Deposit within 21 days of the issue of the letter of acceptance of the tender, so that the contract is secured before supplies commence.

q: The AAC of an item is 7,200 units. The stock in hand is 1,400 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 700 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Coverage = (stock in hand + dues) / AAC x 12 = (1,400 + 700) / 7,200 x 12 = 3.5 months.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 7,800 units and its Economic Order Quantity is 650 units. If the cost of placing one order is Rs 140, the total ordering cost per year is:
e: Orders per year = annual requirement / EOQ = 7,800 / 650 = 12; total ordering cost = 12 x Rs 140 = Rs 1,680.

q: A 'trial' (developmental) order is placed on a new firm, which has not so far supplied an item to the Railways, primarily in order to:

options.A: Meet the annual procurement target from new firms
options.B: Assess the firm's capability and the quality of its product before bulk orders are placed on it
options.C: Enable the firm to avoid payment of Earnest Money Deposit
options.D: Help the firm in obtaining registration with the Railways

e: A trial (developmental) order is placed on a new firm in a limited quantity primarily to assess the firm's capability and the quality of its product before bulk orders are placed on it.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 36 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.14 crore and issues during the year are Rs 1.02 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance of stores = opening balance + receipts - issues = Rs 36 lakh + Rs 1.14 crore - Rs 1.02 crore = Rs 48 lakh.

q: The average consumption of an item is 185 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 6 weeks. The consumption of the item during the lead time is:
e: Lead time consumption = average consumption per week x lead time in weeks = 185 x 6 = 1,110 units.

q: In connection with stores consignments received at a depot, 'demurrage' charges, as distinct from 'ground rent', are payable for:

options.A: Storage of rejected material in the depot beyond the stipulated period
options.B: Keeping purchased scrap in the depot beyond the delivery period
options.C: Occupying office accommodation in the depot premises
options.D: Detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for unloading them

e: Demurrage is payable for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for unloading them; ground rent, by contrast, is charged for keeping material or scrap on railway premises beyond the permitted period.

q: A depot holds 500 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 30 per unit. Fresh receipts of 300 units at Rs 36 per unit and 200 units at Rs 42 per unit are taken into stock. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised book (average) rate = (500 x Rs 30 + 300 x Rs 36 + 200 x Rs 42) / 1,000 = Rs 34,200 / 1,000 = Rs 34.20 per unit.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 8,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 2 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5% of the value of stores in arrear for each week of delay = 0.005 x Rs 8,00,000 x 2 = Rs 8,000.

q: Insurance (capital) spares required for a new item of equipment are ordinarily procured:

options.A: Along with the procurement of the main equipment itself
options.B: Only after the equipment is commissioned
options.C: Only when the equipment first breaks down
options.D: From the scrap released from similar equipment

e: Insurance (capital) spares for a new item of equipment are ordinarily procured along with the procurement of the main equipment itself, so that the essential spares are available when the equipment enters service.

q: The re-order level of an item is 2,600 units. The average consumption is 160 units per week and the average lead time is 9 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum stock level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 2,600 - (160 x 9) = 2,600 - 1,440 = 1,160 units.

q: During stock verification, 16 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 275 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Value of the excess = units found excess x book rate = 16 x Rs 275 = Rs 4,400, taken into stock with credit to the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: Under the General Financial Rules, the Security Deposit taken from a successful tenderer to secure the due performance of a stores contract is referred to as:
e: Under the General Financial Rules, the Security Deposit furnished by the successful tenderer to secure the due performance of a stores contract is referred to as Performance Security, EMD being the Bid Security.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 63 lakh and its Turnover Ratio is 0.21. The total issues of stores during the year are:
e: Total issues = closing balance / Turnover Ratio = Rs 63 lakh / 0.21 = Rs 3 crore.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 800 units and a safety stock of 250 units. The inventory carrying cost is Rs 12 per unit per year. Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the annual carrying cost of the average inventory held (cycle stock plus safety stock) is:
e: Average inventory = EOQ/2 + safety stock = 800/2 + 250 = 650 units; annual carrying cost = 650 x Rs 12 = Rs 7,800.

q: In e-tendering for stores through IREPS, a tenderer who has submitted his bid may modify or withdraw the bid:

options.A: At any time before the opening of the tenders, even after the due date
options.B: At any time before the due date and time fixed for submission of tenders
options.C: Only within one hour of submitting the bid
options.D: Not at all, once the bid is submitted

e: In IREPS e-tendering, a tenderer may modify or withdraw his bid at any time before the due date and time fixed for submission of tenders; thereafter the bid stands locked for opening.

q: The AAC of an item is 8,400 units. Coverage for five months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 850 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 650 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Quantity to order = requirement for 5 months - stock - dues = (8,400 x 5/12) - 850 - 650 = 3,500 - 1,500 = 2,000 units.

q: The safety (buffer) stock of an item is 380 units and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 18 per unit per year. The annual carrying cost attributable to the safety stock is:
e: Annual carrying cost of the safety stock = safety stock x carrying cost per unit = 380 x Rs 18 = Rs 6,840.

q: Firms registered with the NSIC are, as a rule, exempted from payment of Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders. The abbreviation NSIC stands for:
e: NSIC stands for National Small Industries Corporation; firms registered with the NSIC are, as a rule, exempted from payment of Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 1.75 crore. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 14 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual inventory carrying cost = average stock value x carrying cost rate = Rs 1.75 crore x 14% = Rs 24.5 lakh.

q: A depot holds 2,100 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 95 to Rs 88 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = quantity in hand x fall in book rate = 2,100 x (Rs 95 - Rs 88) = 2,100 x Rs 7 = Rs 14,700, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 700 units and a safety stock of 180 units. Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the average inventory of the item held is:
e: Average inventory = EOQ/2 + safety stock = 700/2 + 180 = 350 + 180 = 530 units under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 90 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 6 crore. The stock held in the depots represents, broadly, issues for a period of:
e: Stock in terms of issues = (closing balance / total issues) x 12 = (Rs 90 lakh / Rs 6 crore) x 12 = 1.8 months of issues held in the depots.
